sweep:model.notes:
RECOMMENDED ARCHITECTURE ('tamborkit', one T4, ~60–100 min production; 'teste' preset ≤ 15 min). All runtimes are [U] until benchmarked in cell 1.

1) Separation of time scales [D]: contact ~ms (DEM dt 0.3–0.4 ms) ≪ flame/flue ~s ≪ lifter period/rotation 15–150 s ~ freeboard gas residence 1–4 min < shell τ_w 3–10 min ≪ batch 2.2–2.9e4 s (6–8 h). Every block uses its own clock. The batch driver advances on the slow clock (dt 0.25–1 s); faster blocks enter as quasi-steady maps or phase-locked replays.

2) DEM keyframes (existing dem.py, PyTorch, soft linear spring-dashpot + Coulomb + rolling resistance; coarse 'waste parcels' 60–90 mm, D/d ≥ 25):
- 4–5 charge states, s = remaining solid volume/initial. (a) Fresh, wet, loose charge (F 0.3–0.5). (b) Hot, sticky, compacting at 120–250 °C: capillary + lubrication force of Vo et al., η from rheology.py. (c) Melt pool + inerts (sand, glass, metals, organics): the DEM is replaced by the existing 2D Stokes/Brinkman pool with a rimming wall film, h* = √(μU/ρg) from the brief. (d) Char/coke + inerts bed at F 0.05–0.15.
- Each state: 2–3 revolutions in a periodic slab of L/6 (0.6–1.8 min/rev at 1.5e7–5e6 particle-steps/s), plus one full-drum 2–3 rev run for the video.
- Outputs, phase-binned over the lifter period: u(x), φ, granular diffusivity D_g (from MSD), dynamic angle, covered arc 2ε, wall-contact time distribution, curtain fraction, Lacey rate, torque. Optionally the Markov matrix P.
- Clumps: only for the look (bottles and rope as 2–5 sphere clumps cost ~3×).
- DEM does NOT carry heat or chemistry. If a thermal DEM demo is wanted, use BOB + MPMH correction + PFP, because plastics are gas-gap dominated.

3) Bed thermal/chemistry (the long run):
- Eulerian 2D cross-section slices (y, z), 160² (gpu) or 128² (test), 4–8 axial slices batched in one tensor (burners are not axially uniform). Semi-Lagrangian advection on the phase-locked keyframe velocity (lab-frame steady for rolling), dt 0.25 s → 1e5 steps for 7 h ≈ 7 min [U].
- Physics: enthalpy method with melting; water evaporation plateau (wet marine litter: a ~100 °C hold that delays oil, essential in the live plot); RS-L2 kinetics HDPE/LDPE/PP/PS + PET + PVC (HCl) + biomass/organics; char yields from PET, biomass, PVC and filler; a wall 'coke index' ∫m(T>550 °C)dt.
- Wall heat transfer: the brief's sub-grid penetration wall layer (h_ws series with χ). Radiosity between free wall, bed surface and curtains. Gas-bed convection.
- Re-key the velocity field as s and the melt fraction cross thresholds; blend between keyframes over ~1 lifter period.
- Cross-check: a Markov-chain bed (about 1e3 cells, 7 h in seconds), also used for sweeps (rpm 0 vs rotating; lifters vs none).
- Precedents: Tsotsas/Kwapinska (DEM ↔ penetration model equivalence), rCFD (~100×) and Markov models (~100×). Verification: rotation has a weak effect on conduction-dominated heating (Chaudhuri, Adepu, Zhang 2022); Nafsun mixing times in the brief.

4) Shell: 2D (θ, x) transient, implicit, dt 1 s, rotating through the furnace map q_f(x, θ_lab). Insulated casing losses. Gives T_w(x, θ, t) for the bed slices and the freeboard. With rpm 0 the same model shows the static hot-spot hazard (Hedlund P4O, in the brief).

5) Furnace/combustion:
- Visual: a low-Mach LES of the firebox (flarekit: mixture fraction + β-PDF equilibrium tables via Cantera, soot/radiation) at 2–3 firing states, a few seconds each.
- Coupling: a quasi-steady table q_f(x, θ_lab; P_fire, T̄_shell, fuel mix aux/NCG) from time-averaged LES or a steady flamelet solve, valid because τ_flame ≪ τ_rev < τ_w ≪ τ_batch.
- Batch control as the plant runs it: burner modulates to hold 500 °C (bed or gas setpoint) with a firing cap. NCG from the condenser train is recycled to the burner, so the auxiliary fuel falls once gas production starts (a second live trace).

6) Freeboard 3D: low-Mach RANS/SST (Gr ~1e10–1e11, so not laminar) on 64×64×192 [U], quasi-steady at 6–8 keyframes (~2 min each [U]), interpolated in time.
- Inputs: vapour/steam sources from the bed slices, the rotating shell wall T, the cold front door, the rear outlet and rotary joint.
- Scalars: Option-B cracking, gas age, wax dew point vs wall T (Riazi) and a reflux return term to the bed (Dobó 2020 shows reflux shifts the split).
- Key KPI: the residence-weighted freeboard T. '70 % oil' implies ≲ 550 °C (Option B: 13 % cracked at 550 °C vs 82 % at 600 °C over 150 s).

7) Live plot and video: the batch driver logs cumulative oil (condensed W+O after freeboard cracking and reflux), gas, char mass, mean bed T, shell max T, NCG vs auxiliary fuel and the moisture left.
- The video is a time-lapse: the 3D drum shows the DEM keyframe motion (real speed loops) with the charge state, colour (T, melt, char) and fill level interpolated in s; the plot advances in batch time.
- On-screen disclosure: 'movimento: DEM em quadros-chave; calor/química: modelo contínuo acoplado (não é DEM de 7 h)'.

8) Rejected alternatives (justified):
- (i) Full CFD-DEM for the whole batch: 6–60 h of DEM alone on a T4 [D], and Star-CCM+ needs 21.6–46.2 h per 15 s [TC]. DEM also breaks down once the plastic melts.
- (ii) Coarse-grained thermal DEM through the whole batch: parcels of mixed waste have no defined k ratio for the heat-scaling laws, and the cost is still 20–300 h.
- (iii) Heat-capacity/time scaling (Chaudhuri-style): acceptable for verifying heating curves but invalid with Arrhenius chemistry tied to absolute time.
- (iv) TFM/KTGF: rejected in the brief (dense frictional bed, no closure for melt-coated solids).
- (v) Pure 0D/1D: cannot show the visuals, the freeboard cracking or the static-vs-rotating hot spots.

9) Runtime budget [U]: setup and benchmark 3–5 min; DEM keyframes 15–30 min; bed slices 7–20 min (+ Markov sweeps 1–2 min); shell negligible; freeboard keyframes 12–20 min; furnace LES visual 10–20 min; SDF render and HD video 10–15 min. Total ≈ 60–110 min. Keep checkpoints, because Colab sessions can disconnect.

GAPS / CAVEATS:
- No PyTorch or Taichi DEM benchmark was found; measure it.
- The Liu–Dai–Li 2026 method is unreadable (paywall, null abstract).
- No validated DEM of melting plastic in drums exists.
- The coarse-grain heat-law exponents come from PDF text extraction (check the superscripts). The LMLB formula as printed in DEMLab is dimensionally odd.
- Drum dimensions D 2.2 × 6 m and charge 2–3 t are placeholders [H] pending the geometry thread (Beston model of the UFRJ unit).
- The freeboard/cracking numbers depend on Option B [C] and the molar-mass assumption (60–100 g/mol).
- The rCFD and Markov speed-ups are from fluidized beds and tablet coaters, not kilns.
- New derivations are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Programacao/381db60a-cc64-54cc-aefe-1e483b5b217d/scratchpad/r5calc/r5.py.

- IVIG's 'based on technologies used in BLJ-16 type systems' wording, the lab description and CO2/NaOH capture.

- The spoken claims in the video (500 °C, about 70 % oil, 6-8 h).

Corrections:
1. The UFRJ '70 % oil' should not be the base case for Guanabara-Bay litter. Keyhani et al. 2025 (Applied Energy 401:126759, full text) gives marine-litter oil of 16-65 wt%, mostly 45-55; gas 20-30 wt%; solids 20-30 wt% (>50 wt% when non-plastics dominate). Faussone 2021 got about 45 wt% from Venice Lagoon litter.
2. The Fr regime band 'Fr < 1e-4 slumping' is unsourced and misattributed to Henein. A DEM validation (arXiv:2009.10448) shows rolling at Fr 1e-4 to 1e-3, and granular maps do not apply to film/melt charges anyway.

5. The FAQ's 180 °C onset is tyre-specific; Beston says plastic runs 'a little higher'.
6. Beston Turkey's 60 kg/h fuel is a running-cost item, not explicitly preheat.
7. The torque estimate's r_cg varies from 0.14 to 0.41 D with fill, giving 0.67-1.92 kN·m; the conclusion is unchanged.
8. The video size estimate is biased upward: the mouth ring is a lower bound on drum ID.

- 2 x 200,000 kcal/h burners: not on any fetched Beston page or case page. Scaling the BLJ-20 preheat fuel by shell area gives about 0.26-0.68 MW, so use 0.3-0.7 MW.
